articles.title: Tolan snags $30M for its AI companion that helps users navigate life
articles.snippet: Tolan snags $30M for its AI companion that helps users navigate life TechCrunch
articles.text:
Tolan , the AI companion designed to help people manage their daily lives, navigate relationships and emotions, and accomplish their goals, has just expanded its runway with another $30 million in capital.
The startup’s investors in the latest round include Union Square Ventures, Khosla Ventures, and Homebrew, doubling the total amount it has raised to date and pushing its valuation beyond the previous $120 million, according to a new report by Upstarts Media . (The startup didn’t disclose its new valuation, but PitchBook estimates it at more than $268 million, with “medium confidence.”)
Users engage with Tolan’s app through a cartoonish character that’s meant to offer support and help them get through their to-dos.
Image Credits: Tolan on App Store
Tolan generates revenue from its tiered memberships, which are required for full access to all features. The company told Upstarts Media its annual recurring revenue is now in the “double-digit millions.”
The startup is one of the few AI companions that have found some traction, as it claims to have more than 250,000 active users who have had more than 70 million conversations over the past year. Around 70% of its users are women, and 40% are parents, Tolan’s team told the news outlet. (Anecdotally, the app is said to appeal in particular to neurodivergent people , who may benefit from additional support, whether that’s emotional support or help with organizing tasks.)
Compared with other companions, Tolan seems to have found a balance between being helpful without being perceived as too weird. Compare that with the public shaming that Friend’s pendant-based AI companion faced; users dubbed Friend “ very cringe ,” The New York Times called it “hated,” and Wired said it “has no soul.”
Meanwhile, another former top contender in the space, Character.AI, recently filed for bankruptcy after its founder’s return to Google . (Its remaining staff is transitioning to Disney, which bought some of its assets.)
However, Tolan could end up facing increased competition from the more recent crop of AI agents, which help users plan, organize, and accomplish their tasks and goals, not just talk their way through them. For instance, Meta gave its AI agent Muse a cute avatar for its users to talk to, which it also plans to release as a hardware product in the future.
The startup also has to navigate the risks of offering AI-powered emotional support, given that multiple lawsuits have been filed against general-purpose AI app makers alleging that chatbot interactions contributed to users’ suicides.

articles.title: RapidCanvas Raises $29M Series B to Bring Fortune 100-Grade AI to Every Enterprise
articles.snippet: RapidCanvas Raises $29M Series B to Bring Fortune 100-Grade AI to Every Enterprise GlobeNewswire
articles.text:
Home /
Newsroom / Press Releases October 16, 2026
RapidCanvas Raises $29M Series B to Bring Fortune 100-Grade AI to Every Enterprise
Led by Vertex Ventures SEA & India with participation from Hitachi Ventures, the round will scale RapidCanvas’ Hybrid Approach™, pairing its AI platform with field AI engineers.
AUSTIN, Texas, Oct. 16, 2026 - RapidCanvas , the managed AI execution company pioneering the Hybrid Approach to deliver custom AI solutions at SaaS economics, has raised $29 million in Series B funding led by Vertex Ventures SEA & India with participation from Hitachi Ventures. Existing investors Accel, Peak XV Partners, Valley Capital Partners and Titanium Ventures also participated in the round. The financing brings total funding to $52.5 million. The raise follows 8x growth in annual recurring revenue over the past six quarters as enterprises demand outcomes from custom AI in production. More than 40% of RapidCanvas’ customers now run multiple AI use cases in production.
RapidCanvas pairs its AI platform with field AI engineers to deliver custom AI solutions. AI engineers learn each customer’s business processes, design and build custom AI applications, and stay accountable for the applications’ outcomes after delivery. The RapidCanvas AI platform brings together three products: The Enterprise Context Engine™ lets an enterprise capture how a business process runs, from requirements and tribal knowledge to data schemas and decision history, and the enterprise owns that context. The Visual Development Canvas lets AI engineers rapidly build custom AI solutions that meet industry benchmarks, drawing on a skills library that gives each new solution a 60% head start from proven, benchmarked code. The Operational Harness manages and governs AI solutions once they’re deployed in production. RapidCanvas offers its Hybrid Approach at subscription pricing, changing the economics of enterprise AI.
So far in 2026, more than 75 enterprises in manufacturing, financial services, retail, business services and infrastructure have made 1.4 million AI-led decisions with applications built on RapidCanvas.
“AI can be the great equalizer, but so far its biggest wins have gone to the Fortune 100. We want to give every enterprise the same opportunity,” said Rahul Pangam, co-founder and CEO of RapidCanvas . “Vibe coding has made it easy to start building with AI. Getting AI into production reliably and safely still remains the biggest gap. Our growth over the past six quarters is evidence that AI in enterprises is moving beyond pilots into production and real operations.”
RapidCanvas serves an underserved market: enterprises with $100 million to $10 billion in revenue that have AI budgets and C-suite mandates but no proven path to outcomes. These companies are caught between services firms that charge millions and take months to deliver, and do-it-yourself platforms that require specialized AI talent most of them don’t have. In conversations with more than 400 business leaders, RapidCanvas found that most C-level executives expect a return on AI within six to 12 months, yet very few have moved beyond pilots and proofs of concept.
“Most enterprises are still searching for real returns on their AI spend. RapidCanvas delivers them by pairing an AI platform that compounds with every deployment and field AI engineers who own the outcome end to end. AI Firm RapidCanvas Raises $29 Million For Global Expansion

AI-managed services firm RapidCanvas, with a strong presence in India, has successfully raised USD 29 million in Series B funding, led by Vertex Ventures SEA and India, to fuel its global expansion and product innovation.
Key Points
AI-managed services firm RapidCanvas secured USD 29 million (approximately Rs 275 crore) in Series B funding on Friday.
The funding round was led by Vertex Ventures SEA and India, with Hitachi Ventures and existing investors also participating.
This fresh financing takes RapidCanvas's total funding to USD 52.5 million.
RapidCanvas plans to use the funds to expand its go-to-market teams and network of private equity and advisory partners.
The company will also grow its employee base in India and its field AI engineering team across India, the US and Brazil, alongside investing in product development.
AI-managed services firm RapidCanvas, which has the majority of its employees based in India, on Friday said it has raised USD 29 million or about Rs 275 crore in a funding round led by Vertex Ventures SEA and India.
Funding Details And Investors
The latest funding round also saw participation from Hitachi Ventures and existing investors, including Accel, Peak XV Partners, Valley Capital Partners and Titanium Ventures.
"RapidCanvas, the managed AI execution company pioneering the hybrid approach to deliver custom AI solutions at SaaS economics, has raised USD 29 million in Series B funding led by Vertex Ventures SEA & India," the company said in a statement.
The fresh financing takes total funding in the company to USD 52.5 million.
Strategic Growth And Product Investment

The company will use part of the fund to grow its employee base in India as well.
